status: Pre-outcome plan for one public-design feasibility pilot; not a systematic review or preregistration
question: Does replacing linear consultation fee with unrestricted observed fee levels create structural aliasing in an independently released healthcare DCE?
dataset: BRAC University CHORUS Bangladesh DCE, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19478777
inclusion_reason: Public deidentified choice data, documented block/menu structure, three actual consultation-fee amounts, and a codebook. Selected without examining outcome associations.
core_model: Two facility alternative constants; categorical medicine/treatment cost, waiting time, provider, referral and service scope; consultation fee linear in BDT100
expanded_model: Replace linear consultation fee with indicators for BDT200 and BDT300, reference BDT100, only on active facilities
primary_checks: unweighted residual information for the extra fee-curvature direction
restrictions: Medicine/treatment cost codes mean free/half/full, not currency amounts; never sum these codes with consultation fees
Do not infer random allocation or causal effects from an archive description alone
A full-rank result is not a power or sample-quality guarantee
A deficient result is not evidence against all D-efficient designs
Classic design ranks and nuisance-adjusted information remain classical results
No human response records are redistributed without verifying the source license
publication_role: One external feasibility audit can test a research direction; it cannot establish general prevalence, an independently new method or submission readiness.
